item.title: The Holiday Season Is Doing Something to Your Body. Here's What It Is.
item.description: Financial pressure, disrupted sleep, sugar, alcohol, overscheduling. Each one raises cortisol on its own. Stack them for six weeks and your body is running in a low-grade stress state almost continuously.
item.content:encoded:
The holidays are one of the most reliable cortisol triggers of the year. Financial pressure, disrupted sleep, sugar, alcohol, overscheduling -- each one raises cortisol on its own. Stack them together and your body is running in a low-grade stress state almost continuously.

item.title: Gratitude Is Medicine: How Your Emotions Affect Your Health
item.description: The emotions you dwell in most often are quietly shaping your health. Here is what the science says about cortisol, chronic stress, and how gratitude works as medicine.
item.content:encoded:
The emotions you dwell in most often are quietly shaping your biology. Chronic negative emotional states raise cortisol, suppress immune function, and accelerate inflammation. Gratitude does the opposite -- and the research is more robust than you might expect.
